decision.explanation: Swapping coordinates preserves scalar multiplication: T(kx,ky)=(ky,kx)=kT(x,y). It also preserves addition: T(x₁+x₂,y₁+y₂)=(y₁+y₂,x₁+x₂)=T(x₁,y₁)+T(x₂,y₂). Thus T is linear, and all three statements are true.

after.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}54 \\ -36 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2}).$
after.worked_solution:
First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2} & =18{v}_{1}+3{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2} \\  & =18({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})+3{v}_{1} \\  & =18(0)+3{v}_{1} \\  & =3{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2})=T(3{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(3{v}_{1}) & =3T({v}_{1}) \\  & =3[\begin{aligned}54 \\ -36 \\ 30\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}162 \\ -108 \\ 90\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

after.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2}).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2} & =13{v}_{1}+13{v}_{2}-5{v}_{2} \\  & =13({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})-5{v}_{2} \\  & =13(0)-5{v}_{2} \\  & =-5{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2})=T(-5{v}_{2}).
$$

 

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-5{v}_{2}) & =-5T({v}_{2}) \\  & =-5[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}40 \\ -20 \\ -45\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}40 \\ -20 \\ -45\end{aligned}].$
